newsitem.title: UK: Chinese mission investigates London stock listing.
newsitem.headline: Chinese mission investigates London stock listing.

text.p: China's Vice-Premier Li Lanqing led a visit of senior officials to the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday to investigate opportunities for Chinese companies to list in London.

"The visit underlines the Chinese government's commitment in this process and we look forward to welcoming Chinese companies to our market," said Gavin Casey, chief executive of the London Stock Exchange.
"We welcome this opportunity to emphasise the benefits of the London market and the international advantages we can offer to Chinese companies looking to list internationally."

The visit follows an agreement between regulatory authorities in London and Beijing last month that allows Chinese companies to be traded in London either through the launch of global depository receipts (GDRs) or via secondary listings.
A stock exchange official said the first listing could take place within a matter of weeks.
"It could be done within three weeks and some companies may have already started preparations," he said.
"The fashion seems to be at the moment, when it's a country that does not have an established trading record, to list GDRs," he added.

London has to compete with the Tokyo and New York stock markets for Chinese listings, but it offers the advantage of a time zone difference over Hong Kong, where Chinese shares are more commonly listed, he said.
London's appeal as the market with the greatest volume of internationally traded stocks may also weigh in any decision, he said.
Analysts say Chinese electricity generator, Datang Power, is likely to be first to take advantage of the memorandum of understanding, signed in Beijing last month.
They predict the issue, which some estimate at $300 to $400 million, will be quoted in London before the year end, though it has also been waiting for a listing in Hong Kong.
China's vice minister of foreign affairs, Zhang Deguang, and Chen Xinhua, vice minister of foreign trade and economic cooperation, were also among the delegation.
